fullPassage:
There is a wealth of evidence that when parents, teachers, supervisors, and coaches are perceived as involved and caring, people feel happier and more motivated. And it is not just those people with power — we need to feel valued and respected by peers and coworkers. Thus, when the need for relatedness is met, motivation and internalization are fueled, provided that support for autonomy and competence are also there. If we are trying to motivate others, a caring relationship is a crucial basis from which to begin. And when we are trying to motivate ourselves, doing things to enhance a sense of connectedness to others can be crucial to long-term persistence. So exercise with a friend, call someone when you have a difficult decision to make, and be there as a support for others as they take on challenges.

For many centuries, humans have taken advantage of tools that translate and bring into our perception natural phenomena that we can't perceive with our senses. In some cases, this consists of simply amplifying signals that feed into our normal sensory inputs (e.g., telescopes can bring into clear view that which is too far away for our eyes to perceive on their own). Other instruments turn signals that we cannot perceive into ones that we can observe. Some of these take the form of expanding the reach of our current senses, such as creating visible images based on the ultraviolet spectrum of light or changing sounds that are normally outside the range of what human ears can hear into audible signals. Alternatively, some instruments measure properties for which we have no sensory capacity at all and change them into that which we can observe.

Science is concerned with accumulating and understanding observations of the physical world. That understanding alone solves no problems. Individual people have to act on that understanding for it to help solve problems. For instance, science has found that regular exercise can lower your risk of heart disease. Knowing this fact is interesting, but it will do nothing for your personal health unless you act on it and actually exercise. And that's the hard part. Reading an article about exercise is easy. Getting into an actual routine of regular exercise is harder. In this sense, science really solves no problems at all. Problems are only solved when people take the knowledge provided by science and use it. In fact, many of humanity's biggest problems are caused by lack of action, and not lack of knowledge.

Many forms of research lead naturally to quantitative data. A study of happiness might measure the number of times someone smiles during an interaction, and a study of memory might measure the number of items an individual can recall after one, five, and ten minutes. Asking people how many times in a year they are sad will also yield quantitative data, but it might not be reliable. Respondents' recollections may be inaccurate, and their definitions of 'sad' could vary widely. But asking "How many times in the past year were you sad enough to call in sick to work?" prompts a concrete answer. Similarly, instead of asking people to rate how bad a procrastinator they are, ask, "How many of your utility bills are you currently late in paying, even though you can afford to pay them?" Questions that seek concrete responses help make abstract concepts clearer and ensure consistency from one study to the next.

Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. In year three, the crops will rotate again. By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order. Each crop enriches the soil for the next crop. This type of farming is sustainable because the soil stays healthy.

Nearly everything has to go through your mouth to get to the rest of you, from food and air to bacteria and viruses. A healthy mouth can help your body get what it needs and prevent it from harm — with adequate space for air to travel to your lungs, and healthy teeth and gums that prevent harmful microorganisms from entering your bloodstream. From the moment you are created, oral health affects every aspect of your life. What happens in the mouth is usually just the tip of the iceberg and a reflection of what is happening in other parts of the body. Poor oral health can be a cause of a disease that affects the entire body. The microorganisms in an unhealthy mouth can enter the bloodstream and travel anywhere in the body, posing serious health risks.

The interaction of workers from different cultural backgrounds with the host population might increase productivity due to positive externalities like knowledge spillovers. This is only an advantage up to a certain degree. When the variety of backgrounds is too large, fractionalization may cause excessive transaction costs for communication, which may lower productivity. Diversity not only impacts the labour market, but may also affect the quality of life in a location. A tolerant native population may value a multicultural city or region because of an increase in the range of available goods and services. On the other hand, diversity could be perceived as an unattractive feature if natives perceive it as a distortion of what they consider to be their national identity. They might even discriminate against other ethnic groups and they might fear that social conflicts between different foreign nationalities are imported into their own neighbourhood.

We tend to believe that we possess a host of socially desirable characteristics, and that we are free of most of those that are socially undesirable. For example, a large majority of the general public thinks that they are more intelligent, more fair-minded, less prejudiced, and more skilled behind the wheel of an automobile than the average person. This phenomenon is so reliable and ubiquitous that it has come to be known as the "Lake Wobegon effect," after Garrison Keillor's fictional community where "the women are strong, the men are good-looking, and all the children are above average." A survey of one million high school seniors found that 70% thought they were above average in leadership ability, and only 2% thought they were below average. In terms of ability to get along with others, all students thought they were above average, 60% thought they were in the top 10%, and 25% thought they were in the top 1%!

As the social and economic situation of countries got better, wage levels and working conditions improved. Gradually people were given more time off. At the same time, forms of transport improved and it became faster and cheaper to get to places. England's industrial revolution led to many of these changes. Railways, in the nineteenth century, opened up now famous seaside resorts such as Blackpool and Brighton. With the railways came many large hotels. In Canada, for example, the new coast-to-coast railway system made possible the building of such famous hotels as Banff Springs and Chateau Lake Louise in the Rockies. Later, the arrival of air transport opened up more of the world and led to tourism growth.

For creatures like us, evolution smiled upon those with a strong need to belong. Survival and reproduction are the criteria of success by natural selection, and forming relationships with other people can be useful for both survival and reproduction. Groups can share resources, care for sick members, scare off predators, fight together against enemies, divide tasks so as to improve efficiency, and contribute to survival in many other ways. In particular, if an individual and a group want the same resource, the group will generally prevail, so competition for resources would especially favor a need to belong. Belongingness will likewise promote reproduction, such as by bringing potential mates into contact with each other, and in particular by keeping parents together to care for their children, who are much more likely to survive if they have more than one caregiver.

Every day, children explore and construct relationships among objects. Frequently, these relationships focus on how much or how many of something exists. Thus, children count — "One cookie, two shoes, three candles on the birthday cake, four children in the sandbox." Children compare — "Which has more? Which has fewer? Will there be enough?" Children calculate — "How many will fit? Now, I have five. I need one more." In all of these instances, children are developing a notion of quantity. Children reveal and investigate mathematical concepts through their own activities or experiences, such as figuring out how many crackers to take at snack time or sorting shells into piles.

The whole of human society operates on knowing the future weather. For example, farmers in India know when the monsoon rains will come next year and so they know when to plant the crops. Farmers in Indonesia know there are two monsoon rains each year, so next year they can have two harvests. This is based on their knowledge of the past, as the monsoons have always come at about the same time each year in living memory. But the need to predict goes deeper than this; it influences every part of our lives. Our houses, roads, railways, airports, offices, and so on are all designed for the local climate. For example, in England all the houses have central heating, as the outside temperature is usually below 20°C, but no air-conditioning, as temperatures rarely go beyond 26°C, while in Australia the opposite is true: most houses have air-conditioning but rarely central heating.

We used to think that the brain never changed, but according to the neuroscientist Richard Davidson, we now know that this is not true — specific brain circuits grow stronger through regular practice. He explains, "Well-being is fundamentally no different than learning to play the cello. If one practices the skills of well-being, one will get better at it." What this means is that you can actually train your brain to become more grateful, relaxed, or confident, by repeating experiences that evoke gratitude, relaxation, or confidence. Your brain is shaped by the thoughts you repeat. The more neurons fire as they are activated by repeated thoughts and activities, the faster they develop into neural pathways, which cause lasting changes in the brain. Or in the words of Donald Hebb, "Neurons that fire together wire together." This is such an encouraging premise: bottom line — we can intentionally create the habits for the brain to be happier.

❌ ② 19세기에 철도는 내륙 산악 지역만을 개방하였다: 철도가 해변 리조트(Blackpool, Brighton)와 산악 호텔 모두 개방. '만(only)' 불일치

❌ ③ 항공 교통의 등장은 세계 관광 성장에 아무런 영향을 주지 않았다: 'the arrival of air transport ~ led to tourism growth' — 관광 성장에 기여했다고 명시. 불일치

✅ ④ 사회경제적 상황이 나아지면서 임금과 근무 환경이 개선되었다: 'As the social and economic situation of countries got better, wage levels and working conditions improved' — 원문과 일치 ← 정답
det.tip: got better → improved: 경제 호황 → 여가 시간 증가 → 교통 발달 → 관광 성장

questions.passage: Every day, children explore and construct relationships among objects. Frequently, these relationships focus on how much or how many of something exists. Thus, children count — "One cookie, two shoes, three candles on the birthday cake, four children in the sandbox." Children compare — "Which has more? Which has fewer? Will there be enough?" Children calculate — "How many will fit? Now, I have five. I need one more." In all of these instances, children are developing a notion of quantity. Children reveal and investigate mathematical concepts through their own activities or experiences, such as figuring out how many crackers to take at snack time or sorting shells into piles.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 아이들은 매일 사물들 간의 관계를 탐구하고 구성한다.
아이들은 세기, 비교, 계산을 통해 양의 개념을 키워 나간다.
아이들은 수학적 개념을 정규 교육 과정에서만 습득한다.
간식 시간에 과자 수를 파악하는 것도 수학적 탐구의 사례에 해당한다.

det.korean: 아이들의 자연스러운 수학적 개념 발달
det.analysis:
❌ ① 아이들은 매일 사물들 간의 관계를 탐구하고 구성한다: 'Every day, children explore and construct relationships among objects' — 일치

❌ ② 아이들은 세기, 비교, 계산을 통해 양의 개념을 키워 나간다: 'children are developing a notion of quantity' — 일치

✅ ③ 아이들은 수학적 개념을 정규 교육 과정에서만 습득한다: 'through their own activities or experiences' — 자신의 활동과 경험을 통해 학습한다고 명시. 정규 교육 과정(formal education) 언급 없음 ← 정답

❌ ④ 간식 시간에 과자 수를 파악하는 것도 수학적 탐구의 사례에 해당한다: 'figuring out how many crackers to take at snack time' — 일치
det.tip: through their own activities or experiences = 정규 교육이 아닌 자발적 활동으로 학습

questions.passage: We used to think that the brain never changed, but according to the neuroscientist Richard Davidson, we now know that this is not true — specific brain circuits grow stronger through regular practice. He explains, "Well-being is fundamentally no different than learning to play the cello. If one practices the skills of well-being, one will get better at it." What this means is that you can actually train your brain to become more grateful, relaxed, or confident, by repeating experiences that evoke gratitude, relaxation, or confidence. Your brain is shaped by the thoughts you repeat. The more neurons fire as they are activated by repeated thoughts and activities, the faster they develop into neural pathways, which cause lasting changes in the brain. Or in the words of Donald Hebb, "Neurons that fire together wire together." This is such an encouraging premise: bottom line — we can intentionally create the habits for the brain to be happier.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 첼로 연주가 뇌 발달에 미치는 구체적 효과
반복적 연습을 통한 뇌 회로 강화와 행복 증진 가능성
뇌가 본질적으로 변하지 않는다는 과학적 근거
Donald Hebb의 뉴런 이론이 지닌 한계점

det.korean: 반복적 연습을 통한 뇌의 변화 가능성
det.analysis:
❌ ① 첼로 연주가 뇌 발달에 미치는 구체적 효과: 첼로는 비유로만 사용. 글의 주제가 아님

✅ ② 반복적 연습을 통한 뇌 회로 강화와 행복 증진 가능성: 핵심 논지. 'specific brain circuits grow stronger through regular practice' + 'we can intentionally create the habits for the brain to be happier' ← 정답

❌ ③ 뇌가 본질적으로 변하지 않는다는 과학적 근거: 글은 이 관념을 반박('this is not true')

❌ ④ Donald Hebb의 뉴런 이론이 지닌 한계점: Hebb의 이론은 글의 논지를 뒷받침하는 인용. 한계점 논의 없음
det.tip: 핵심 문장: specific brain circuits grow stronger through regular practice → intentionally create habits

questions.passage: Science is concerned with accumulating and understanding observations of the physical world. That understanding alone solves no problems. Individual people have to act on that understanding for it to help solve problems. For instance, science has found that regular exercise can lower your risk of heart disease. Knowing this fact is interesting, but it will do nothing for your personal health unless you act on it and actually exercise. And that's the hard part. <u>Reading an article about exercise is easy. Getting into an actual routine of regular exercise is harder.</u> In this sense, science really solves no problems at all. Problems are only solved when people take the knowledge provided by science and use it. In fact, many of humanity's biggest problems are caused by lack of action, and not lack of knowledge.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 "Reading an article about exercise is easy. Getting into an actual routine of regular exercise is harder."가 함축하는 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 운동에 관한 기사를 읽는 것은 시간 낭비에 불과하다.
규칙적인 운동 습관을 들이는 것은 사실상 달성 불가능한 목표이다.
지식을 얻는 것과 그것을 실천에 옮기는 것 사이에는 상당한 괴리가 있다.
과학적 발견은 건강 문제를 해결하는 데 실질적으로 도움이 되지 않는다.

overlay.underline: Reading an article about exercise is easy. Getting into an actual routine of regular exercise is harder.

det.korean: 지식 습득과 실천 사이의 간극
det.analysis:
❌ ① 운동에 관한 기사를 읽는 것은 시간 낭비에 불과하다: 시간 낭비가 아니라 '쉽다'는 것. 읽기의 가치를 부정하는 것이 아님

❌ ② 규칙적인 운동 습관을 들이는 것은 사실상 달성 불가능한 목표이다: '어렵다(harder)'는 것이지 '불가능하다(impossible)'는 것이 아님

✅ ③ 지식을 얻는 것과 그것을 실천에 옮기는 것 사이에는 상당한 괴리가 있다: reading(아는 것) = easy ↔ routine(실천) = harder. 글 전체가 knowledge vs action 대비. 'lack of action, not lack of knowledge' ← 정답

❌ ④ 과학적 발견은 건강 문제를 해결하는 데 실질적으로 도움이 되지 않는다: 행동하면 도움이 된다는 것이 글의 논지
det.tip: reading(아는 것) = easy ↔ routine(실천) = harder → knowledge vs action gap

questions.passage: We tend to believe that we possess a host of socially desirable characteristics, and that we are free of most of those that are socially undesirable. For example, a large majority of the general public thinks that <u>they</u> are more intelligent, more fair-minded, less prejudiced, and more skilled behind the wheel of an automobile than the average person. This phenomenon is so reliable and ubiquitous that it has come to be known as the "Lake Wobegon effect," after Garrison Keillor's fictional community where "the women are strong, the men are good-looking, and all the children are above average." A survey of one million high school seniors found that 70% thought they were above average in leadership ability, and only 2% thought they were below average. In terms of ability to get along with others, all students thought they were above average, 60% thought they were in the top 10%, and 25% thought they were in the top 1%!
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 they가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: they = 일반 대중의 대다수(a large majority of the general public)
det.analysis:
✅ ① 일반 대중의 대다수: 'a large majority of the general public thinks that they are more intelligent ~' — they는 the general public 자신을 가리킴 ← 정답

❌ ② 사회적으로 바람직한 특성들: 특성(characteristics)이 아닌 사람(people)을 지칭

❌ ③ 고등학교 졸업반 학생들: 고등학생 설문은 이후 문장에서 등장하는 별개의 예시

❌ ④ Garrison Keillor의 가상 공동체 주민들: Lake Wobegon은 현상을 설명하기 위한 비유일 뿐
det.tip: thinks that they = 대중이 '자신들이' ~라고 생각한다. they = the general public

questions.passage: For many centuries, humans have taken advantage of tools that translate and bring into our perception natural phenomena that we can't perceive with our senses. In some cases, this consists of simply amplifying signals that feed into our normal sensory inputs (e.g., telescopes can bring into clear view that which is too far away for our eyes to perceive on their own). Other instruments turn signals that we cannot perceive into ones that we can observe. Some of <u>these</u> take the form of expanding the reach of our current senses, such as creating visible images based on the ultraviolet spectrum of light or changing sounds that are normally outside the range of what human ears can hear into audible signals. Alternatively, some instruments measure properties for which we have no sensory capacity at all and change them into that which we can observe.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 these가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 감지 불가능한 신호를 관찰 가능한 것으로 변환하는 도구들

det.korean: these = other instruments(감지 불가능한 신호를 변환하는 도구들)
det.analysis:
❌ ① 우리가 감지할 수 없는 자연현상들: 자연현상은 도구의 대상이지 these가 지칭하는 것이 아님

❌ ② 일상적으로 사용하는 감각 기관들: 감각 기관이 아니라 '도구(instruments)'를 지칭

❌ ③ 자외선 스펙트럼에 기반한 가시적 이미지들: 이미지는 these 뒤에 나오는 구체적 예시이지 these 자체가 아님

✅ ④ 감지 불가능한 신호를 관찰 가능한 것으로 변환하는 도구들: 'Other instruments turn signals that we cannot perceive into ones that we can observe. Some of these ~' — these = other instruments ← 정답
det.tip: these = Other instruments. 바로 앞 문장의 주어를 받는 지시대명사

questions.passage: There is a wealth of evidence that when parents, teachers, supervisors, and coaches are perceived as involved and caring, people feel happier and more motivated. And it is not just those people with power — we need to feel valued and respected by peers and coworkers. Thus, when the need for relatedness is met, motivation and internalization are fueled, provided that support for autonomy and competence are also there. If we are trying to motivate others, a caring relationship is a crucial basis from which to begin. And when we are trying to motivate ourselves, doing things to enhance __________ can be crucial to long-term persistence. So exercise with a friend, call someone when you have a difficult decision to make, and be there as a support for others as they take on challenges.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: a sense of connectedness to others

overlay.blank: a sense of connectedness to others

det.korean: ② a sense of connectedness to others(타인과의 연결감)가 적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① one's personal financial independence(개인적 재정 독립): 동기와 관계성 주제와 무관

✅ ② a sense of connectedness to others(타인과의 연결감): 원문 일치. relatedness(관계성) → motivation. 친구와 운동, 전화, 지지 등 구체적 예시가 뒤따름 ← 정답

❌ ③ individual academic accomplishments(개인적 학업 성취): 관계성이 아닌 개인 성취

❌ ④ complete independence from social bonds(사회적 유대로부터의 완전한 독립): 관계의 중요성과 정반대
det.tip: connectedness to others = 타인과의 연결감. 뒤의 예시(친구와 운동, 전화)가 핵심 단서

questions.passage: The whole of human society operates on knowing the future weather. For example, farmers in India know when the monsoon rains will come next year and so they know when to plant the crops. Farmers in Indonesia know there are two monsoon rains each year, so next year they can have two harvests. This is based on their knowledge of the past, as the monsoons have always come at about the same time each year in living memory. But the need to predict goes deeper than this; it influences every part of our lives. Our houses, roads, railways, airports, offices, and so on are all designed for the local climate. For example, in England all the houses have central heating, as the outside temperature is usually below 20°C, but no air-conditioning, as temperatures rarely go beyond 26°C, while in Australia the opposite is true: most houses have air-conditioning but rarely central heating.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 인도의 농부들은 몬순 시기를 알고 작물 심는 시기를 결정한다.
인도네시아에서는 매년 두 번의 몬순으로 두 번의 수확이 가능하다.
영국 주택에는 대부분 중앙난방과 에어컨이 모두 설치되어 있다.
호주 주택은 대부분 에어컨을 갖추고 있지만 중앙난방은 거의 없다.

det.korean: 날씨 예측과 기후에 따른 생활 설계
det.analysis:
❌ ① 인도의 농부들은 몬순 시기를 알고 작물 심는 시기를 결정한다: 'farmers in India know when the monsoon rains will come ~ they know when to plant the crops' — 일치

❌ ② 인도네시아에서는 매년 두 번의 몬순으로 두 번의 수확이 가능하다: 'Farmers in Indonesia know there are two monsoon rains each year, so ~ two harvests' — 일치

✅ ③ 영국 주택에는 대부분 중앙난방과 에어컨이 모두 설치되어 있다: 'all the houses have central heating ~ but no air-conditioning' — 에어컨이 없다고 명시. 불일치 ← 정답

❌ ④ 호주 주택은 대부분 에어컨을 갖추고 있지만 중앙난방은 거의 없다: 'in Australia ~ most houses have air-conditioning but rarely central heating' — 일치
det.tip: 영국: 난방 O + 에어컨 X / 호주: 에어컨 O + 난방 X → 정반대

questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 과학적 지식이 문제 해결로 이어지려면 실천이 필수적이다
운동이 심장 질환 예방에 미치는 긍정적 효과

det.korean: 과학적 지식과 실천의 관계

❌ ② 과학적 발견이 이루어지는 과정과 원리: 글은 발견 과정이 아닌 지식 활용을 다룸

❌ ③ 운동이 심장 질환 예방에 미치는 긍정적 효과: 운동은 예시일 뿐, 주제가 아님

questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. In year three, the crops will rotate again. By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order. Each crop enriches the soil for the next crop. This type of farming is sustainable because __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: farmers can grow more varieties of crops
crop prices remain stable throughout the year

det.korean: ② the soil stays healthy(토양이 건강하게 유지된다)가 적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① farmers can grow more varieties of crops(농부들이 더 많은 종류의 작물을 재배할 수 있어서): 다양성이 아닌 토양 건강이 지속 가능성의 이유

✅ ② the soil stays healthy(토양이 건강하게 유지된다): 원문 일치. 'Each crop enriches the soil for the next crop. This type of farming is sustainable because the soil stays healthy.' ← 정답

❌ ③ crop prices remain stable throughout the year(작물 가격이 연중 안정적이어서): 가격 관련 내용 없음

❌ ④ weather patterns become more predictable(날씨 패턴이 더 예측 가능해져서): 날씨와 무관한 토양 건강 주제
det.tip: enriches the soil → soil stays healthy → sustainable. 윤작의 핵심 원리

questions.passage: For creatures like us, evolution smiled upon those with a strong need to belong. Survival and reproduction are the criteria of success by natural selection, and forming relationships with other people can be useful for both survival and reproduction. Groups can share resources, care for sick members, scare off predators, fight together against enemies, divide tasks so as to improve efficiency, and contribute to survival in many other ways. In particular, if an individual and a group want the same resource, the group will generally prevail, so competition for resources would especially favor a need to belong. Belongingness will likewise promote reproduction, such as by bringing potential mates into contact with each other, and in particular by keeping parents together to care for their children, who are much more likely to survive if they have more than one caregiver.
questions.stem:
다음 글에 따르면, 집단은 자원을 공유하고 아픈 구성원을 돌보며 적을 상대로 함께 싸우고 과업을 분담하여 어떤 것을 향상시키는가? 본문에서 찾아 영어로 쓰시오. (7단어)

_________ _________ _________ _________ _________ _________ _________
questions.wa: divide tasks so as to improve efficiency
accept: divide tasks so as to improve efficiency

det.korean: 과업을 분담하여 효율성을 향상시키다(divide tasks so as to improve efficiency)
det.analysis:
본문: 'divide tasks so as to improve efficiency' — 집단이 과업을 분담하여 효율성을 향상시킨다

핵심 구문: so as to = ~하기 위하여 (목적의 부정사구)
det.tip: divide tasks so as to improve efficiency = 과업 분담 → 효율성 향상. 집단의 생존 이점 중 하나
